**Working entry:** Bundled fonts — a run's fonts bundled from the stand's DejaVu Sans; `fonts-unavailable` kept; every
CI OS reads one state, never compared by shot bytes (v030-14).

**Capability:** v030-14 — «A run's fonts are bundled, so two hosts read the same state the same way»; acceptance
«Hosts of different operating systems read one state of a run the same way, compared by its readings, not by image
bytes.» Intent §9 (C3): randomness and fonts depend on the host; a run's fonts are bundled so two hosts read the same
state the same way — the trust layer under auto-exploration's replays.

- A run's text is shaped and measured from one bundled font set, the stand's DejaVu Sans
  (`examples/seven_guis/assets/DejaVuSans.woff2`), with the host's system fonts off, on every path a run boots through:
  the stand's boot, the driver session's served tasks, the shared fixture pages and a harness-built document that names
  no font context of its own. [inferred] — today the stand and its fixtures already build `build_single_font_ctx(DEJAVU_SANS)`
  (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:58-60`), while `HarnessOptions::font_ctx` defaults to `None`, which
  `BaseDocument::new` turns into the system collection under the `system-fonts` feature
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:464-486`, `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:27-42`); which run paths
  still read host fonts is P3's to measure.

- The generic families a run's styles name (`sans-serif`, and whatever `serif` / `monospace` / an unknown family resolve
  to) reach the bundled set and not the host. [inferred] — whether fontique maps a generic family onto a lone
  registered font with system fonts off is P3's to measure.

- `fonts-unavailable` is kept: an app whose font context holds no family it can paint text with is still refused
  before anything is painted or read (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:31`, `screenshot.rs:30`).

- The proof: every CI OS (the `test` leg's Linux, macOS and Windows runners) reads one state of a run the same way,
  compared by its readings — the snapshot text, bounds, text extents, lint findings — never by a shot's bytes (a shot's
  PNG bytes already differ between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64, CLAUDE.md §Architecture). [inferred] — how a
  cross-OS comparison is held in CI (a committed reading each OS replays, or a kept check) is P3/P4's to settle.

body:
# Adapting 0.3.0's planned work to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (the escher overseer's reconnaissance, 2026-10-29)

**Why.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас
стоит адаптировать с учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать
изза новых требований». The 0.4.0 plans are in `canvas-and-node-graph.md`: virtual nodes inside a canvas, the canvas
observed as data, a `drag` verb, and pan and zoom through a transform.

**Read at `a6c6a37c7`**: `escher-0.3.0/requirements.md`, `working-route.md`,
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, and `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`,
`command.rs`, `wire.rs`. These are the overseer's reading of the code, not measurements.

## What already fits (no rework expected)
- **The snapshot is built from the accesskit tree** (`snapshot.rs:98`: «its id and role from that tree»). That tree
  carries non-DOM nodes natively, so a canvas's virtual nodes can enter it without a new carrier.
- **An action lands on a point.** `click` and `type` press the centre of the target's bounds
  (`execute.rs:360`, `:427-439`). A virtual node with bounds can be clicked the same way, as long as the canvas app
  hit-tests its own pointer events.
- **The wire is versioned** (`wire.rs:37`, `v3`), so a new verb is an additive, versioned change.

## Where 0.3.0 could build something 0.4.0 would have to redo
1. **The stable-id grammar** (`element_id.rs`). Today an id is an author key, an anchored path (`//`), a component path,
   or a document path (`/…`), all derived from DOM and vdom elements. A virtual node has no DOM element. If D2, B3,
   E2's recorded checks and replay store ids in this grammar, 0.4.0 needs a form for `{canvas element}` + `{virtual
   key}` that collides with none of the four. **Adapt in «The UI graph» (v030-05): reserve that form now (a separator no
   current id can hold), even if nothing produces it yet.**
2. **The node model of the UI graph and of «What can I do here»** (v030-05, v030-06). If the graph and the actionable
   list are keyed on a DOM element (`Target.node: NodeId`, `execute.rs:354`), a virtual node does not fit. **Adapt: key
   them on the agent-visible node (the accesskit node with its bounds), with an optional owner element, and let a
   handler sit on an owner element and serve sub-targets.** A canvas typically has one listener that dispatches inside.
3. **Verbs as a closed list in B3 and E2** (v030-06, v030-09). If «What can I do here» and auto-exploration hard-code
   `click`/`type`/`press`/`scroll`, adding `drag` (two points or a node plus a destination) means reshaping both.
   **Adapt: read the per-node verbs from the schema's verb table, and let the recorded-check step format carry verbs
   with more than one target, versioned.**
4. **Handler coverage** (v030-07) counts DOM listeners. A canvas's internal handlers are invisible to it. **Adapt:
   state that limit in its acceptance, so 0.4.0 extends it rather than redefines it.**
5. **Layout explained** (v030-11) reads Taffy and Stylo. A virtual node's place is the app's own. **Adapt: let its
   answer name the "placed by the app inside canvas X" case, so the field set is not closed.**
6. **Bundled fonts** (v030-14). Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) must draw from the same bundled fonts, or a canvas reads
   differently across hosts. **Adapt: in its acceptance, name canvas text as a reader of the bundled set.**
7. **Engine debts** (v030-04). The transform `visible_region` fix should be proven on a pan/zoom container like the
   node graph's (`canvas-and-node-graph.md`).

## What 0.3.0 should not take on
The canvas renderer itself, the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap, `drag`, and virtual-node production all stay in 0.4.0.
The adaptations above keep 0.3.0's shapes open; they add no 0.4.0 capability.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-14-bundled-fonts · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-14T08:33:33Z

A run's fonts are already bundled: every path a run boots through — the session host's `start`, `mcp` and `coverage`
roles, a kept check's replay and the shared fixture pages — takes `stand::options`, whose font context is the stand's
DejaVu Sans with system fonts off (research §Graph impact, 94 call sites; scope rev 4, premise corrected). What no check
holds is v030-14's outcome: that hosts of different operating systems read one state of a run the same way. Today only
the two committed Counter checks replay on linux, windows and macOS (`stand_replay.rs`, research §Patterns), so the
Counter is the one screen whose cross-OS equality anything measures.

This chunk adds that measurement and changes no production code. A new stand check boots each of the six served tasks
as the session host boots them, in both layout modes, reads each screen through the driver — `snapshot` (every part),
`lint` and `actions` — at boot and after one acting step reached by clicks or typed text, and holds the driver's own
`answer_digest` of every answer (the digest a kept check keeps, `packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs:41`) equal to
one committed table. The test leg (linux x86_64) and `matrix_test` (windows x86_64, macOS aarch64) each read that one
table, so a green run on all three is the cross-OS reading; no shot is compared
(`(architecture · decision/no-screenshot-in-cross-os-byte-check)`). A second check holds the generic families a run's
styles can name on the bundled set: `serif`, `monospace`, `system-ui` and an unavailable family read the text extent
`sans-serif` reads, and `cursive` and `fantasy` are measured.

`fonts-unavailable` is kept unchanged — its readers (`execute.rs:592`, `lint.rs:224`, `screenshot.rs:76`) and its five
witnesses stand (research §Graph impact, query 3). The canvas adaptation (inputs#I2, inputs#I3 §6) is met by naming
canvas text as a future reader of the bundled set in v030-14's acceptance: the set is the document's own font context
(`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:464-488`), the one every glyph run laid out in the document is shaped from
(`packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs:34`); the canvas renderer itself stays 0.4.0 (inputs#I3 §What 0.3.0 should not take
on).

1. **The cross-OS readings check** — create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cross_os_readings.rs` (keeps arch S1–S3,
   tests S1–S4, obs S1, a11y S2, layouts S1–S2, design S1–S2). Its `//!` names the behaviour: each served task reads one
   state the same way on every OS the tests run on, compared by the driver's answer digests, never by a shot.
   - The session: each of the six served tasks — `counter`, `flight-booker`, `timer`, `crud`, `cells`, `load` — held
     in process through `session_common::hold` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs:39-41`, which boots
     through `stand::options`, the boot the session host uses at `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:46-52`), once
     with incremental layout and once without.
   - Its precondition first (arch S1): the held app can paint text — a `lint` call is accepted, not refused
     `fonts-unavailable`.
   - The readings, each through `Session::run` and digested by `escher_driver::answer_digest`: `snapshot` with no part,
     and on a screen over the budget every `snapshot --part n` from 1 to its `parts`; then `lint`; then `actions`.
   - Read at boot, then once more after one acting step per task, each reached by `click`, `type` or `advance` alone —
     never `press` (a key the editor compiles out on macOS reaches no cross-OS state, test-plan history n=18):
     Counter, one click on its increment button; Flight Booker, a `type` of a valid return date into the return field
     after choosing the return flight by `type` on `flight-type`; Timer, `advance` 1000 ms; CRUD, a `type` into the
     name and the surname fields, then a click on Create; Cells, a click on one cell, then a `type` of a number into
     it; Load, a click on its load button (the in-process `LoadNet` answers within the act's load wait). The ids are
     the ones the session checks' shared tables already name (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`,
     `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`); a step whose answer is refused fails the check.
   - The table: one `const` array of rows `(task, moment, verb, part, digest)`, its row count asserted (tests S4),
     the digests written as 16-hex literals measured on the dev host under the workspace build, and asserted equal in
     both layout modes — the two modes are held equal by `stand_boot`'s
     `incremental_and_full_layout_boots_lay_out_identically` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_boot.rs:78-79`); a row the
     two modes read apart is not split into two rows but stops the step (see Implementation notes).
   - A failure names the task, the moment, the verb, the part and the layout mode — never a digest, an id, a name or
     a reading (tests S4, `(test-plan · decision/refusal-leaves-instance-unchanged)`); the file prints nothing, reads no
     env var, sleeps on nothing and reads no wall clock (obs S1, tests S3).

2. **The bundled families check** — create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_bundled_font_families.rs` (keeps arch S1–S3,
   tests S1–S4, obs S1, design S1, layouts S2). A fixture page of its own (one reader, tests S2: it stays in the file),
   booted through `fixtures::boot` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs:19`, the stand's options), both layout
   modes: one inline-root element per family holding the same short Latin text at one size, set in `sans-serif`,
   `serif`, `monospace`, `system-ui`, an unavailable named family, `cursive` and `fantasy`.
   - Its precondition first: the `sans-serif` element's text extent (`BaseDocument::text_extent`,
     `packages/blitz-dom/src/text_extent.rs:25`) is non-zero.
   - Asserted: `serif`, `monospace`, `system-ui` and the unavailable family each read the `sans-serif` element's text
     extent — equal width and height — since `build_single_font_ctx` appends the one font to those three generics and
     `sans-serif` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:153-162`) and an unavailable family falls back to the initial `serif`
     (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/font_family_fallback.rs:7-17`).
   - `cursive` and `fantasy` — not registered by `build_single_font_ctx` — are measured, then asserted as read: equal to
     `sans-serif`'s extent where they read it; where either reads otherwise, the check asserts what it reads, its `//!`
     states it as a stated limit of the bundled set, and the implement report names it for the wrap's residual and its
     line in `escher-0.4.0-incubator/deferred-from-0.3.0.md` (inputs#I1). Predicted: both read `sans-serif`'s extent —
     record what the measurement reads.

3. **Measure the table** — run the cross-OS check once on the dev host under the workspace build
   (`cargo test --workspace --locked --test stand_cross_os_readings`) with the table's digests unset, read each
   reading's digest from the check's own failure path in a scratch run (never printed by the committed file), write
   the 16-hex literals into the table, and re-run green under the workspace build and the per-package build
   (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_cross_os_readings`). The two builds compile blitz-dom with
   different features, `writing-mode` among them (test-plan history n=14, n=15); the digests must hold under both.

4. **Controls, red before green** (tests S4, `decision/mutation-controlled-tests`), each through `gate.py control` and
   recorded in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-14-bundled-fonts/evidence/`:
   - cross-OS check, the table's hold — one digest literal's last hex digit flipped in the check's table: the check
     reads red, naming that row's task, moment, verb, part and mode, and green again restored.
   - cross-OS check, the font's reach — `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:60`'s `build_single_font_ctx(crate::DEJAVU_SANS)`
     replaced by `FontContext::default()` (fontique's default collection, the host's system fonts): predicted red on
     the first `snapshot` row at boot — record what the control reads; a green reading says the dev host's
     `sans-serif` is the same face at the same metrics, recorded as such, and the digest flip stands as the check's
     red.
   - families check — `build_single_font_ctx`'s `Serif` append removed (`packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:153-162`): the
     `serif` row reads red. Restored, the tree reads green.

5. **Hold the rest unchanged** — run the existing `fonts-unavailable` witnesses and the readings this chunk could
   only disturb by a mistaken production edit (the guard entry asserts none was made): `stand_act_screenshot`,
   `stand_lint`, `stand_actions`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `stand_replay`, `stand_snapshot_text`, `stand_boot`, under the
   fast leg.
6. **The local pre-push gate** — `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cross_os_readings.rs` — the six served tasks' readings at boot and after one step, both layout modes, held to one committed table of `answer_digest`s
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_bundled_font_families.rs` — the generic families a run's styles can name read on the bundled set, on a fixture booted with the stand's options
- none — no production file, manifest, CI workflow, committed check or master (research §Files to modify)

The gates run on the dev host, Linux. Nothing boots outside the harness: there is no live leg, and the real boot is
/implement P3's. The base sha in the guard entry is HEAD as this plan is written,
`557f1c98d4e5639ec7e065025d092feda234b3b7`.

v030-14's acceptance needs CI: the windows and macOS readings exist only on `matrix_test`'s «Test (windows)» and «Test
(macos)» jobs, and the linux one on the `test` leg; so the plan carries the operator's hygiene, push and CI-read
entries, the CI read asserting `verdict: green`. «Stand checks repeated» runs both new `stand_` files three rounds
(the glob, test-plan `decision/stand-checks-repeated-three-rounds`). No dependency and no production code change, so
the audit and coverage legs are no local entry: CI runs them and the CI read covers them.

- Stand checks live in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_{boot,counter,flight_booker,timer,crud,element_ids,id_persistence,accessibility_ids,snapshot,snapshot_state,snapshot_text,diff,id_edits,actionable_keys}.rs`, each building its harness through `stand::boot` (or `Harness::from_vdom` with `stand::options` — for a fixture page through the shared `fixtures::boot` of `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` — for Home, the edit fixtures, the state fixture — a checkbox, two radios and a password input the lean tasks lack — the text check's two fixtures, a password input and a file input, and the diff check's three — a panel hidden by attribute, a password input and a label a button rewrites) and driving it with the harness input helpers: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --test stand_boot` (etc.). They assert unconditionally under the bundled font — no font skip, no sleep, no `dispatch_recorded`. Since 2026-10-14-quality-gates the `stand-repeat` CI leg (not a fast leg) runs every `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs`, one `--test` each, and, on the same line, seventeen named blitz-tests targets outside that prefix as literal `--test` words (`stand_requirement_sweep`'s `STAND_REPEAT_NAMED` still holding the first ten), each file keeping its name, in three rounds — a zero-failure budget, no retry, no `--ignored`.
